short: Patterson's bias for cubic Gauss sums

title.title: Patterson's bias for cubic Gauss sums, unconditionally
title.subtitle: Claim: summed over primes, normalized cubic Gauss sums grow like $\tfrac{6}{5} c_* X^{5/6}/\log X$, with no GRH

lines.tex: \sum_{N\pi \le X} \tilde g(\pi) = \tfrac{6}{5}\, c_*\, \frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X} + o\Big(\frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X}\Big)

beats.text: Each normalized Gauss sum has size 1; with random signs their sum would stay small
Schematic, constants dropped: the bias is a power $X^{1/6}$ below the trivial size
Patterson conjectured it in 1978; it was known only assuming GRH

achievement.label: Patterson's conjecture (1978)
achievement.context: Before: proved assuming GRH (Dunn and Radziwill, 2021)

verify.detail: In Lean: the first moment, angular comparison and angular cancellation
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean docs and allowed axioms; we did not build it

sources.quote: sum over primary Eisenstein primes pi with N(pi) <= X of the normalized cubic Gauss sum G(pi) equals (6/5) c_* X^{5/6}/log X + o(X^{5/6}/log X), with c_* = (2 pi)^{2/3}/(3 Gamma(2/3))
Patterson (1978) conjectured the X^{5/6} bias. Dunn-Radziwill (2021, arXiv:2109.07463) proved Patterson's conjecture assuming GRH.
Uses the same cubic-theta machinery as the quasi-RH family (003)
main theorem formalized (PattersonFirstMoment: first moment, angular comparison, angular cancellation).
only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` for every family here

plain: Sums attached to primes look like random arrows on a circle, but lean slightly one way, as predicted

voice.text: Patterson's bias for cubic Gauss sums.
Each Gauss sum has size one. Random signs would cancel, yet a slight bias survives.
Patterson predicted it in nineteen seventy-eight.
Claimed: Patterson's bias, now with no unproved hypothesis.
